title: Oddball Onboarding Reminders and Quirky Notes
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview:

This is an intentionally informal, slightly silly companion document to the official onboarding checklist. It lives in scratchpad because some of these notes are purely cultural or useful only to folks who like to ask "where did they hide the spare HDMI?". Use with discretion.

Purpose:
- Capture oddball-but-useful local knowledge that helps new hires settle in faster.
- Offer a few lightweight rituals and office norms that are not in the formal handbook.
- Surface small operational tips that save time (e.g., where the spare dongles live, how to reset the office espresso, who to ping for a standing desk).

Quick intro (1 paragraph):
New hires should complete the canonical onboarding checklist first (HR/IT/Manager items). After the essentials, skim this doc for practical pointers and local flavor. It's intentionally casual — things change often and not everything here is official policy.

Table of Contents:
1. Office practicalities
2. Daily rituals and unwritten norms
3. Tech and desk tips
4. Emergency and first-aid oddities
5. Small procedures and who-knows-what

1) Office practicalities
- Key locations:
  - Snacks/communal fridge: small freezer shelf labeled "donut concessions" (please replace what you take).
  - Spare HDMI / dongles: labeled bag in meeting room B cabinet (top shelf).
  - Print toners and stationery: supplies closet, second shelf, behind the green plant box.
- Kitchen/coffee notes:
  - Espresso machine: short press of the silver button, then long press to purge steam. If it makes a high squeal, flip the red switch behind the unit (ask Facilities if unsure).
  - Refrigerator etiquette: label your food with name + date. Food older than 7 days goes to "community science" (i.e., compost).

2) Daily rituals and unwritten norms
- Standups: 9:30am sharp for most engineering squads; if you are late, DM your squad lead rather than interrupting the thread.
- Meeting rooms: toggle "Do Not Disturb" on the door if you need private whiteboard time; otherwise move to the lounge.
- Lunch culture: Taco Tuesday is unofficial but highly encouraged. If you win the taco duty raffle, you own one pack of hot sauce.

3) Tech and desk tips
- Spare power strip: under the "tool cart" by the big ficus (yes, that ficus).
- Desk plant care: water weekly (small cup), rotate to the window side every two weeks. The office plant-care rota lives in Confluence: company-handbook/office-plant-care.
- VPN quirks: if your private deployment demo fails to reach staging, try toggling the lightweight VPN profile (Profile: redwood-lite) before opening a ticket. This sometimes clears stale routes after laptop sleep.
- Local dev trick: ssh-agent sometimes gets confused after laptop lid suspend. Run: 
  ```
  eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"; ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa
  ```

4) Emergency and first-aid oddities
- First-aid kit: top drawer in reception desk — bandages, antiseptic wipes.
- AED: wall by the main stairs, second floor. The AED signage is slightly faded; we will replace by Q3 but for now note the location.
- If the fire alarm tests at 9:02am: this is usually a scheduled alarm test on Wednesdays; if it occurs outside normal maintenance windows, follow evacuation procedure and report to Safety Lead.

5) Small procedures and who-knows-what
- Printer jam ritual: open back door, gently pull paper toward you, then press the big green "reset" button for 3s. If the jam persists, email facilities@redwood.com and include a photo.
- Lost access badge: temporarily use the visitor kiosk (reception) and submit an IT ticket for a replacement.
- Secret donut stash (team lore): if you find it, leave a note. If you don't find it, don't ask where it is.

Appendix: Practical checklists
- New-hire first-day checklist (short, not exhaustive):
  1. Badge pickup at reception
  2. Laptop checkout + enroll in device management
  3. Join team Slack channels and say hi in #intro
  4. Add calendar blocks for 1:1 with manager and buddy lunch
  5. Visit kitchen, find coffee sequence, and test espresso (quietly)

- Who to ping for things (quick reference):
  - Facilities: facilities@redwood.com
  - IT device issues: it-support@redwood.com
  - People Ops / onboarding logistics: people-ops@redwood.com

Notes and disclaimers:
- This page is intentionally informal and is not a policy document. If you find something that should be official (e.g., a safety correction), please create a Confluence page in the appropriate space and flag People Ops.
- If you have additions, drop them into the comment thread on the Confluence scratchpad page and tag @Priya Shah.

Change log:
